abbrev Def1 := Set ArithmeticSentence

def Def5 (K : Def1) (F : ArithmeticTheory) : Prop := K = F.theory

def Def6 (K : Def1) : Prop := ∃ F : ArithmeticTheory, F.RE ∧ Def5 K F

translation: Def1 is an abbreviation for the type of all sets of closed arithmetic sentences. For a set K of such sentences and an arithmetic theory F, Def5(K, F) means that K equals the set of all theorems of F: for every arithmetic sentence σ, σ belongs to K if and only if σ is derivable from the axioms F. Def5 does not require F to be recursively enumerable. For a given K, Def6(K) means that there exists an arithmetic theory F whose axiom set is recursively enumerable and whose set of theorems is exactly K. The same F must work for every sentence. K need not equal the axiom set F, and neither consistency nor truth in the standard model is required.

divergences.description: Def5 gets the equality right but does not require F to be effectively axiomatized. For example, if K and F are both the set of all true arithmetic sentences, then Def5 K F holds, even though no recursively enumerable axiom set has K as its theorem set. Thus Def5 alone is too broad for Koellner’s notion of a formal system. Def6 repairs this by requiring F.RE.

Def1 supplies a type for K, not a distinguished set of absolutely provable sentences. Reading a particular K as the output of the idealized human mind is an interpretation of the parameter, not something the definition establishes.
The target fixes the language to first-order arithmetic and uses classical first-order derivability. The quoted passages speak of sentences and provability without explicitly fixing that scope.

Koellner’s F_e denotes a theorem set indexed by a natural number; Lean’s F denotes the axiom set and F.theory its theorem set. Quantifying directly over recursively enumerable axiom sets preserves WMT, since each such set has an index. The target does not represent a particular machine code or the knowledge of coincidence used in the stronger theses, neither of which WMT requires.

judgement.summary: Def6 faithfully captures WMT within the chosen language: one effectively axiomatized system must have exactly K as its theorem set. The material mismatch is in Def5 taken on its own, where the same equality can hold for a system with no effective presentation.
